grf.observed_anchor: The owner-fixed product boundary requires exactly one executable EntityOS with no mandatory companion runtime files. Current production uses a one-file packaging path, while future embedded native helpers could otherwise pressure the sidecar boundary.
grf.generated_reality: Linux memfd-backed execution can provide a no-persistent-sidecar mechanism for an embedded helper while preserving the one-file release boundary.
grf.counter_reality: The kernel/runtime may require a filesystem-resident executable path, making memfd execution unavailable or unreliable even on the supported Linux class.
grf.falsifier: Load the bytes of a harmless existing ELF into memfd, execute it through /proc/self/fd/<n>, and require the child marker plus zero exit status; compare with a direct-exec baseline.

unusual_experiment.name: ENTITYOS_MEMFD_EMBEDDED_HELPER_EXECUTION
unusual_experiment.environment: isolated local ChatGPT container; Linux 6.18.35 x86_64; Python 3.13.5; no VPS/self-hosted/production execution
unusual_experiment.mechanism: os.memfd_create -> write ELF bytes -> executable fd -> execve(/proc/self/fd/<fd>)
unusual_experiment.rollback: child exited; anonymous memfd lifetime ended with process; no persistent runtime mutation

implication.retained: memfd/fd-backed execution is a plausible optional Linux adapter for future embedded EntityOS helpers without a mandatory persistent companion file
implication.not_promoted: This does not prove current EntityOS uses or needs memfd, does not prove compatibility with the accepted deployment kernel, and does not replace canonical ClayCode/TypedIR/ClayVM effect semantics.
